Does a model or fit have context-dependent (nonlinear) matrix cells?

Source: R/ctContextDependence.R
ctModelIsNonlinear.Rd

A ctsem matrix cell may be an expression of a latent process or a time dependent predictor, such as DRIFT[1,1] = '-log1p(exp(param)) * eta2'. Such a cell has a value only at a given state and set of predictor values, so summaries and plots report the point at which they evaluated it.

Usage

ctModelIsNonlinear(x)

Arguments

x

A ctStanModel, ctStanFit or ctJuliaFit.

Value

Logical.

Details

References to the state that carries an individually varying parameter (with intoverpop='augmented') do not count, since these are parameters, reported exactly.

Examples

# FALSE: no cell of the bundled fit's model reads a latent state or a time
# dependent predictor.
ctModelIsNonlinear(ctsemtestfit)

# TRUE for a model in which the auto effect of eta1 changes with eta2.
model <- ctModel(LAMBDA = diag(2), manifestNames = c('Y1', 'Y2'),
  latentNames = c('eta1', 'eta2'), PARS = c('a|-log1p_exp(param)', 'b'),
  DRIFT = matrix(c('a + b * eta2', 'drift21', 0, 'drift22'), 2, 2))
ctModelIsNonlinear(model)
